title: The Living Mountain Spring (Ka Umpohliew)
cultural_context: Poetic reflection on the natural fresh-water spring (Umpohliew) as the source of village sustenance and spiritual truth, from 'Ki Sur Ba Dang Sawa'.

khasi: Ka umpohliew ba tuid na poh u maw,
Ka khuid, ka thiang, ka pyngngad;
Kam ju thait ban ai la ka um
Sha man uba wan ba thngan bad ba sliang;
Ki kynthei ki wan tong um ha ki kum,
Ki samla ki shong ban kynud sur;
Sur ka jingsuk ba u Blei u la ai.
english: The freshwater spring flowing from beneath the rock,
It never wearies of offering its waters
Unto every traveler who arrives thirsty and faint;
Village women come with clay pitchers to draw water,
Youths sit by its edge humming songs;
A melody of peace bestowed by God.

khasi: Kum kane ka um to kan long ka dohnud,
Ba theh ka jingbha sha uba bun;
Khlem ka sarong, khlem ka jingrhah,
Ban shakri ia la ka jaidbynriew;
Wat la ngi don ha kjat u lum,
Lada ngi khuid kum ka umpohliew,
Ka jingim jong ngi kan pynim
Ia kiwei pat kiba don ha ka jynjar.
english: Like this living stream, let our inner hearts be,
Pouring forth kindness unto all around;
Free from conceit, free from greed,
Serving with modesty our native people;
Though our dwelling be at the foot of the hill,
If we remain pure as the freshwater spring,
Our lives shall bring healing and renewed hope
Unto those weighed down by sorrow and distress.
